Q: How can I start learning C as a complete beginner? A:

If you're a total beginner I think C Programing: A Modern Approach is a great read. Free to read on the link. There are exercises available at the end of each chapter.

If you keep up and do a good chunk of the proposed exercises you'll end with a really good grasp and ready to jump to advanced topics.

Q: `fatal error: glib.h: No such file or directory` when compiling with gcc A:

In my opinion, you shouldn't even need to know where glib.h is installed. On Linux, msys, etc, you can resort to using the pkg-config utility. That will tell you where to find both the include paths for the headers of glib, but also the right linker commands to link your program together. So say you have a program myprog that uses glib and gtk you could do the following:

gcc -o program program.c $(pkg-config --cflags --libs glib-2.0)

You could just run pkg-config --cflags or pkg-config --libs to see what it outputs, the command above uses the output of pkg-config to provide the right flags to gcc to compile your program.

Q: How to have a setup chunk both in the parent and a child document? A:

The solution to this problem is to include the following in the parent document ABOVE the chunks that bring in the child documents:

options(knitr.duplicate.label = 'allow')

Thus:

---
title: "Case studies of rodents native to South America"
author: "W. Apse"
date: "2026-02-04"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

options(knitr.duplicate.label = 'allow')
```
